blocks.text: To write to a file, open it in write mode "w" and use write(); this replaces the old contents. To add to the end without overwriting, open it in append mode "a".

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
with open("example.txt", "w") as file:
....file.write("As-Salaam-Alaikum, World!\n")

with open("example.txt", "a") as file:
....file.write("Appending new line.\n")

blocks.prompt: What does example.txt contain after both blocks run?
blocks.explanation: Two lines: "As-Salaam-Alaikum, World!" and "Appending new line."

items: "w" overwrites, "a" appends; use file.write(text); \n starts a new line.
